name: Facet
text: Use Playwright MCP to drive EXCAVA in a single browser engine—Chrome. This guarantees fast, consistent rendering and avoids cross-browser quirks that slow us down. The trade-off is locking to Chrome, but since EXCAVA’s interface is Chrome-first anyway, we gain speed and reliability without real loss.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Chrome-only automation risks hiding EXCAVA’s interface breakage in Firefox or Safari—users won’t see the cracks until they switch engines. Better alternative: run Playwright MCP against Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit nightly to catch cross-engine quirks early; settle the argument by measuring rendering lag and bug reports across all three.

name: Facet
text:
Run Playwright MCP against Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit nightly. This catches cross-engine quirks early, ensuring EXCAVA’s interface stays visible and reliable for all users—not just Chrome ones. The trade-off is slower automation and higher resource cost, but early detection prevents bigger failures later.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Running nightly against three engines burns cycles chasing ghosts—most EXCAVA users never touch Safari or Firefox, so we’re optimizing for the wrong failure mode. Better: run Chrome + one secondary engine (Firefox) nightly, log only the deltas, and settle the argument by measuring how often cross-engine bugs actually bite real users in the next sprint.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Run Playwright MCP nightly against Chrome and Firefox only, logging cross-engine deltas to catch real breakage without wasting cycles on WebKit.

Result: A nightly report showing which EXCAVA interface elements differ between Chrome and Firefox, owned by the visualization team.
